headline: Totals Went Perfect, Moneylines Went Looking For Trouble
paragraphs: Twelve games got graded for real, the model passed on five, and the twelve plays it did fire came back 7-5 for a profit of 17.54 on 120 staked. That is a 14.6 percent return, which is the kind of week nobody writes a song about and everybody quietly takes. The three markets, however, did not arrive at that number together.

Totals went 3-0 for 27.27, a 90.9 percent return, and the best of them was Over 50 in South Alabama's neighborhood, no, in San Antonio, where UTSA beat South Florida 31-24 at a 72 percent model number. The same game also produced the week's dumbest moment: South Florida moneyline at plus 215, advertised with 15.9 probability points of edge while the model itself only gave it a 48 percent chance to win. It bet on something it expected to lose. It lost. Moneylines overall went 1-4 for minus 27.

The published top five contained two plays, went 1-1, and made three dollars, a feature that is becoming its own running joke. Season to date across three honestly graded weeks: 66-80-3, down 136.75 on 1,490 staked, a negative 9.2 percent return against a model that keeps insisting it should be hitting 60.2 percent. Strip out the hindsight week and it is 40-25-1 and up 110.47, which is exactly the sort of arithmetic a losing operation loves to mention.
